questions.q:
From the given options, identify the sentence which is in the positive degree.

(SSC MTS 2024 S.51_05-Nov_Shift-1)
o: His brother is an intelligent boy.
I have a greater idea in this regard.
They are playing hockey with longer sticks.
She is the most beautiful girl of the class.
questions.s:
Answer: a) His brother is an intelligent boy.

Explanation:
The positive degree is the base form of an adjective, used when no comparison is being made.

  • "Intelligent" is in the positive degree → simply describes without comparing (बिना तुलना के गुण बताना)

  • "Greater" = comparative degree (तुलनात्मक)

  • "Longer" = comparative degree

  • "Most beautiful" = superlative degree (सर्वोत्कृष्ट)

Only option (a) uses the adjective in the positive degree.

questions.q: You must make a choice immediately because there is few time left.
questions.s: Explanation:- (c) use ‘little’ instead of ‘few’ kyunki 'few' ka use countable noun ke sath kiya jaata hai aur 'time' ek uncountablenoun hai isliye 'little' ka use hoga.

questions.q:
Choose the correct form of adjective for the given sentence:
_______of living life on his own terms, he made few compromises.
questions.s:
Desirous of” is the correct adjective phrase meaning “wanting/keen to do something.”
So the correct sentence is: Desirous of living life on his own terms, he made few compromises.

questions.q: This is (a) / the more beautiful (b) / painting in the collection. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). Use 'most beautiful' for superlative. Answer: (b). Superlative ke liye 'more' nahi, 'most beautiful' chahiye. Jawab: (b).

questions.q: Kunal looked very (manliness) in his police uniform.
questions.s:
We need an adjective to describe how Kunal looked.
manly = adjective meaning “strong and masculine”

questions.q: (a) Having been found /(b) guilty of the theft /(c) Sunny was sentenced to five year’s imprisonment. /(d) No error
(a) The police arrived and discovered /(b) a large number of hoarded sugar/(c) in his shop. /(d) No error
questions.s: SUGAR Uncountable So, Use LARGE QUANTITY in place of LARGE NUMBER.

questions.q: A journey by car is (a)/ as quick or perhaps quicker (b)/ than the one by train. (c)/ in this particular case (d)/ No Error (e)
questions.s: Should be "as quick as, or perhaps quicker than".

questions.q: My Both hands were covered in paint after the art class.
o: My Both hands were
after the art class
questions.s:
The correct option is (b) "My Both hands were."

In English, the word "both" comes before the possessive form. Therefore, "My" should come after "Both"

The corrected sentence should be: "Both my hands were covered in paint after the art class."

questions.q:
With tear eyes, she said goodbye to her dear friend.

{SSC CPO 11/11/2022 S2}
questions.s: The correct phrase is "teary eyes," which describes eyes filled with tears. "Tear eyes" is incorrect in this sentence.

questions.q: It is unlikely that you will (a)/ find more qualified and experience (b)/ candidate than Mr. Prasad (c)/ for the post of president. (d)/ No error (e)
o: It is unlikely that you will
questions.s: Use "qualified and experienced candidate" - both should be past participles.

questions.q: My younger sister (1)/ is much smarter (2)/ then me. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.s: Replace 'then' with 'than'. A comparative degree is followed by 'than'.

questions.q: For example, the parent mountain / of Mont Blanc, the / high peak in the Alps, is the Mount Everest. (SSC MTS Tier-01 16/06/23)
o: high peak in the Alps, is the Mount Everest.
questions.s: Since it refers to a specific, unique peak, the superlative 'highest' is required.

questions.q: The Indian way (a) / of thinking is superior (b) / to most of the (c) / countries of the world. (d) / no error (e)
o: of thinking is superior
to most of the
countries of the world.
questions.s: Should be "superior to that of most of the countries".

questions.q: Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’.
o: fast than smart
more fast than smart
faster than being smart
questions.s:
The correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence is No substitution.

The sentence "He is faster than smarter" is already grammatically correct and conveys the intended meaning.

questions.q: The view is (a) / very much beautiful (b) / from here. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Much' is redundant; correct form is 'very beautiful.' Answer: (b). 'Much' extra hai, sahi form hai 'very beautiful.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: These days, job opportunities are not as better (1)/ as they used to be (2)/ in the early 70's. (3)/ No error (4)
o: These days, job opportunities are not as better
questions.s:
After “as…as”, we use the positive degree of the adjective.
Replace "better” with “good”.

questions.q: It turned out to be the noisy park party anybody had ever attended. (SSC CGL Tier-02 08/08/22)
questions.s: When implying the highest degree, the superlative adjective 'noisiest' should be used.

questions.q: This book is (a) / as good, if (b) / not better than that book. (c) / no error (d)
o: not better than that book.
questions.s: Correct form: "as good as, if not better than".

questions.q: Although the patient (a) was rudely with the (b)/ nurses, he behaved nicely with the doctor. (d) No Error
o: was rudely with the
nurses, he behaved nicely with
questions.s: Use "was rude with" (adjective) not "rudely with" (adverb).
